title: Cover crops raise steady-state infiltration on two contrasting loam soils

headings.text: Cover crops raise steady-state infiltration on two contrasting loam soils

key_sentences: Winter cover crops are promoted as a way to improve soil structure, but field evidence on their effect on infiltration remains mixed.
Across both sites, a rye and vetch mixture increased infiltration by 61 percent relative to bare fallow in the second year.
Cover crops sown after the main harvest keep the soil covered over winter and add roots and residues that may stabilise aggregates.
Both sites had been managed under conventional tillage with a cereal rotation for at least ten years before the trial began.
Measurements were made at three random points per plot, avoiding wheel tracks.
On the silt loam, all three cover crops increased infiltration in both years, and the gap to bare fallow widened in the second year.
Mixtures combining a cereal with a legume may also benefit from the additional biological activity supported by nitrogen-rich residues.
Cover crops raised steady-state infiltration on both soils, and the effect grew between the first and second year.
